merger_name: New England Motor Group – Armidale Automotive Group

acquirers.name: NEW ENGLAND MOTOR GROUP PTY LIMITED

party_page.name: New England Motor Group Pty Limited

merger_description:
Houma Holdings Pty Ltd (**Houma**) proposes to acquire an independently-owned motor vehicle dealership and farm machinery business consisting of Armidale Ford, Armidale Isuzu Ute, Armidale Kia, Armidale Honda, Armidale Nissan, Armidale Kubota, and Armidale 4 x 4 (the **Acquisition**), currently owned and operated by Armidale Automotive Group Pty Ltd (**Armidale Automotive Group**). Armidale Automotive Group is a new and used car retailing business that operates a franchised automotive dealership in Armidale. Armidale Automotive Group also supplies manufacturers’ spare parts and accessories, aftermarket servicing and repairs, and finance and insurance solutions.

The Acquisition will occur via New England Motor Group Pty Ltd (**New England Motor Group**), of which Houma is an 80% shareholder. New England Motor Group operates a motor vehicle dealership at 121 Marsh Street, Armidale, NSW. The dealership represents 2 vehicle brands as an authorised dealer of new vehicles, being Mazda and Suzuki.

Houma is the majority shareholder of a new and used vehicle retail business operating 12 franchised dealerships across locations on the Central Coast, Newcastle, Hunter Region, Tuncurry, Taree, Dubbo, Armidale, Grafton, Boat Harbour and Gympie (the **Houma Dealerships**). The Houma Dealerships represent 22 vehicle brands as an authorised dealer of new vehicles. The Houma Dealerships also sell a range of used vehicles, in addition to providing vehicle servicing and repairs, genuine manufacturers’ spare parts and accessories sales as well as facilitating finance, insurance and customer care products in connection with the vehicle transactions.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has considered the
information provided with the notification waiver application and had
regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Act.
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers it is likely that, if the Acquisition were put into effect, the
notification thresholds would be met.
The ACCC is unable to reach a view that the Acquisition would not
be likely to raise competition issues in any market based on the
information provided, given:
a. the Acquisition would combine the largest dealership of
new cars in the local Armidale region of NSW with one of
only four alternative new car dealerships in that region
b. the merged entity’s combined share of supply of new
cars in the Armidale region of NSW may be significant
c. there is uncertainty regarding the extent to which the
merged entity would be likely to face inter-brand
competition from alternative dealerships in the Armidale
region and the surrounding areas more broadly.
The ACCC considers that the Acquisition warrants consideration
through the notification process, including further information
gathering and consultation with third parties.
Given the above, the ACCC has determined not to make the
notification waiver determination applied for.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
